title: Pipe Bender vs Tube Bender: Which One Do You Actually Need?
excerpt: Pipe bender vs tube bender: how NPS pipe and OD tube differ, why a ram pipe bender kinks tubing, and which bender fits your project.

notes: Research was done through web-search result summaries only: direct page fetches (harborfreight.com, manuals.harborfreight.com, pro-tools.com, roguefab.com, jd2.com, thefabricator.com, amazon.com) were blocked by the sandbox egress policy. Harbor Freight facts (12 tons / 24,000 lb, 1/2-2 in Sch 40/80, up to 90 deg, six cast dies, 'not intended for thin-wall pipe such as conduit or exhaust') come from the kit fact table plus a search summary of the HF manual; please re-check the manual wording. Schedule 40 OD/wall values (1/2 to 2 in NPS) were confirmed in ArchToolbox search results; wall factors are simple division. SCCA Time Trials material list (seamless/DOM, 4130/T45, Docol R8, no ERW) and 3x centerline bend radius were seen in search summaries of SCCA TT rules (the radius wording came via a motorsportreg.com copy) - re-verify on timetrials.scca.com before publishing. Rogue Fab's bending-types page lists exhaust systems as a ram-bender use, which conflicts with HF's manual for its own model; the article states both. Left out (unverified): HF ram stroke length, Schedule 80 wall values, a forum report of HF kinking 2 in x .120 tube at about 15 deg.
